ischemia induces alterations in the actin cytokeleton in vascular smooth muscle of the renal vasculaure.

ischemia or ischemic-reperfusion induces disarray of F- actin in vascular smooth muscles cells of the kidney, and a similar finding was observed after exposure to hydrogen peroxide in cultured vascular smooth muscles cells.

ischemia or ischemic reperfusion induces disorganization/disarray in the actin cyto-skeleton in vascular smooth muscle of the kidney, and this may be a structural basis for altered renal vascular reac-tivity in postischemia acute renal failure.

a novel mechanism for altered renal vascular reactivities in postischemia ARF.
the structural changes in the renal vasuclar smooth muscle cells after ischemic injury and ischemia-reperfuion injury in a rat model.
the structural basis of ischemia-induced renal vasoconstrictive dysfunction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
disorganization/disarray in F-actin of vascular smooth muscle cells is a common finding in ischemic ARF.

the ischemia-induced alterations in the cytoskeletal architecture of the renal vascular smooth muscle may contribute to the loss of autotransgulation of renal perfusion and the aberrant renal vascular reactivity in ARF.
the disorganization of the F-actin cytoskeleton is a structural basis of the loss of vascular autoregulation in ischemic renal failure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
disorganization of F-actins is a common feature of vascular smooth muscle cells in ischemic ARF.

ischemia/reperfusion injury induces structural damage in the renal vasuculature, and this damage may play a contributary role in the loss in autoregulation and vascular reactivity in the postischemic acute kidney injury.
the actin cyto-skeleton in renal vascular smooth muscles plays a key role in the pathogenesis of postischemic acute renal failure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytoskeleton of smooth muscle cells in the renal vas-cular bed undergoes significant changes after ischemia.

ischemia induces structural damage to the cytoskeleton, particularly the actin cytokeleton, of the renal vasculatures, which is a potential contributor to the loss of renal function in postischemia ARF.

the actin cytoplasmic network in vascular smooth muscle undergoes disorganization/disarray during ischemic injury and that this may play a role in the altered vascular reactivity seen in ischemic ARF.
